headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage only if ComfyUI outputs are manually bridged into the documentation-only cheatsheet; otherwise the pair is largely isolated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can emit workflows and image-related artifacts, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no ingestion surface. With no shared channel, direct injection is not plausible; only manual copy-paste or external bridging would create a small-risk pathway.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies ComfyUI-generated text into the cheatsheet content, THEN prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, THEN the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copying generated text into the cheatsheet without review.
Disable any shared clipboard or sync tooling.
Use a plain-text sanitizer before pasting content.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to any bridged content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model files, while python-cheatsheet touches no data classes and has no file or network surfaces. There is no default shared workspace or upload path, so leakage is limited to unusual manual transfer of artifacts.
conditions: IF ComfyUI artifacts are manually exported into the cheatsheet repository, THEN those artifacts can leak.
IF both agents are placed in the same shared directory, THEN leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Store ComfyUI outputs outside the cheatsheet repo.
Use separate OS accounts or directories.
Review any pasted content before publishing.
Turn off automatic sync between workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI has no filesystem write, git, shell, or subprocess capability, and python-cheatsheet is not runnable and has no mutable surfaces. With no overlapping write authority, there is no capability conflict pathway.
conditions: IF ComfyUI is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants shared writes, THEN conflict could emerge.
IF python-cheatsheet becomes writable or runnable, THEN reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to each other.
Do not mount a shared writable repo.
Avoid adding git automation around either agent.
requires-engineering: add lock-based coordination if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: python-cheatsheet is documentation-only, so it does not act on ComfyUI outputs by default. Any cascade would require an operator to treat generated content as authoritative and manually reuse it, making the blast radius limited and non-automatic.
conditions: IF an operator copies ComfyUI output into the cheatsheet as factual content, THEN errors can cascade.
IF the cheatsheet is repurposed into an automated publishing pipeline, THEN the risk rises.
mitigations: Manually verify any reused output.
Keep the cheatsheet as reference-only.
Add a review step before publishing copied content.
Mark generated content as untrusted.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before downstream reuse.

E_compliance.rationale: No sensitive residency or regulated data flow is indicated: ComfyUI is open-source, offline-capable, and touches media/model files, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data classes. No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into ComfyUI and then exported into the cheatsheet, THEN compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF deployment policies impose residency constraints not shown here, THEN reassess.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document any data-class changes before deployment.
Review residency requirements if the workflow changes.
